title: Pasir Panjang Terminal Oil Spill Incident on 14 June 2024
what_it_is: Pasir Panjang Terminal Oil Spill Incident on 14 June 2024

sections.label: No oil slicks observed
sections.summary: Since 18 June, no oil slicks have been observed along East Coast and Changi, including waters off Changi Naval Base.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Since 18 June, no oil slicks have been observed along East Coast and Changi, including the waters off Changi Naval Base.

sections.label: Vessel allision date and time
sections.summary: The allision between Vox Maxima and Marine Honour happened on 14 June at 2.18 pm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The allision between the vessels Vox Maxima and Marine Honour happened on 14 June at 2.18 pm.

sections.label: Patrol vessel booms deemed unsuitable
sections.summary: MPA's lightweight patrol vessel booms were assessed as unsuitable for the 14 June spill of an estimated 400 tonnes of oil.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Some have asked why MPA did not immediately deploy the containment booms onboard its patrol vessel while waiting for T&T’s vessel to arrive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These lightweight booms were assessed to be unsuitable for dealing with the oil spill incident on 14 June, which was a more serious spill involving the sudden discharge of an estimated 400 tonnes of oil into the sea.

sections.label: Booms at biodiversity sensitive areas
sections.summary: Preventive measures were implemented at biodiversity sensitive areas such as Chek Jawa Wetlands, with around 4,000 metres of oil containment booms deployed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Preventive measures were also implemented at biodiversity sensitive areas such as the Chek Jawa Wetlands at Pulau Ubin, given the potential environmental impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We have deployed a total of around 4,000 metres of oil containment booms.

sections.label: Public notification and oil spread
sections.summary: MPA notified the public at 6.03 pm on 14 June, and SDC observed further oil spread on 15 June at Palawan, Siloso and Tanjong beaches.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: At 6.03 pm that day, MPA notified the public of the allision and oil spill through a media release while it continued to assess and respond to the developing situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Early next morning on 15 June at about 7.00 am, SDC observed the further spread of oil in waters at Palawan, Siloso and Tanjong beaches, cordoned off affected areas and deployed workers to commence clean-up.

sections.label: NEA clean-up at shorelines
sections.summary: NEA started clean-up at about 10.00 am at Labrador Nature Reserve and around 4.00 pm at East Coast Park after oil was observed along shorelines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) started clean-up operations at about 10.00 am at Labrador Nature Reserve and around 4.00 pm at East Coast Park, after oil was observed along the shorelines.

sections.label: MPA media statements
sections.summary: MPA and agencies issued five media statements in the first four days to inform the public and address concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MPA and our agencies had issued five media statements in the first four days of the incident to keep the public informed of the management of the incident and to address key concerns they might have.

sections.label: Ministerial Statements and clarifications
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu and Minister Desmond Lee will make related Ministerial Statements, with clarifications allowed after the third Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister Grace Fu and Minister Desmond Lee will be making related Ministerial Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, I will allow Members to raise their points of clarification on all three Statements after the third Statement.

sections.label: Oil-soaked sand collected
sections.summary: As of 30 June, over 1,200 tonnes of oil-soaked sand and debris were collected and much of the oil slicks removed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As of 30 June, over 1,200 tonnes of oil-soaked sand and debris have been collected and much of the oil slicks on our beachfronts has been removed.

sections.label: VOCs within safe limits
sections.summary: The VOCs detected, including for BTX, have been well within safe limits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The VOCs detected, including for BTX, have been well within safe limits.

sections.label: Final clean-up phase
sections.summary: After phase two, the final phase removes tar balls and inspects for oil stains, expected to take around three months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Once the second phase of cleaning operation is completed, we will move to the final phase where we remove tar balls from the beaches and inspect affected areas for any remaining oil stains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We expect the clean-up to take around three months, but these will vary for each area, depending on the extent they are affected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The cordoned-off area of the beaches at Sentosa, along East Coast Park and Southern Islands will progressively open for land-based activities.

sections.label: Rental deferral measures
sections.summary: The agencies are developing rental deferral measures to help affected businesses with cash flow on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The agencies are developing rental deferral measures to help affected businesses with their cash flow on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: Local and imported fish safety
sections.summary: Test results continue to show that local and imported fish are safe for consumption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The test results continue to indicate that our local fish and imported fish are safe for consumption.

sections.label: Oil pollution clean-up progress
sections.summary: Over 1,200 tonnes of oil-soaked sand were collected and most beachfront oil slicks removed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   We have made good progress in cleaning up the oil pollution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We have collected over 1,200 tonnes of oil-soaked sand and effectively, most of the oil slicks at the beachfront have been removed.

sections.label: Clean-up work duration
sections.summary: The entire clean-up work is expected to take about three months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The entire clean-up work is expected to take about three months.

sections.label: Food safety, water supply, stepped-down measures
sections.summary: Fish farms and water supply were unaffected, and with conditions stabilised, precautionary measures will be gradually stepped down.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In terms of food safety and water supply, our fish farms have not been affected by the oil spill incident.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Our water supply has also not been affected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, in conclusion, as we are now in the second phase of the clean-up operations, some of the precautionary measures adopted in the first phase, such as daily air monitoring at affected beaches and water quality monitoring for our fish farms, have become less pressing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Given that the conditions have stabilised, we will gradually step down measures that are no longer required so that agencies can focus on the current demands.

sections.label: Oil-absorbent booms deployed
sections.summary: NParks deployed over 1.5 kilometres of oil-absorbent booms to protect biodiversity-sensitive coastal and marine areas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: NParks deployed over 1.5 kilometres of oil-absorbent booms to protect biodiversity-sensitive coastal and marine areas, including Berlayer Creek and the Rocky Shore along Labrador Nature Reserve.

sections.label: Collared kingfishers rescued
sections.summary: NParks and animal welfare groups rescued four collared kingfishers from the oil spill, two received by NParks' Centre for Wildlife Rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As of end-June, NParks and animal welfare groups, such as ACRES, have rescued four collared kingfishers from the oil spill, two of which were received by NParks' Centre for Wildlife Rehabilitation.

sections.label: Oil spill volunteer sign-ups
sections.summary: Over 1,500 people signed up to help with oil spill management, and over 700 volunteers were deployed as of 1 July.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: More than 1,500 individuals have signed up to help with oil spill management efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As of 1 July, we have deployed over 700 volunteers, including volunteers from the Public Hygiene Council (PHC), and Friends of Marine Park.

sections.label: Recovery efforts after safety assessment
sections.summary: In the next six months and beyond, once NEA assesses affected areas as safe, recovery efforts like coastal clean-ups and beach patrols will be done with partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In the next six months and beyond, once NEA has assessed the affected areas to be safe for public access, we will work with our partners on recovery efforts, such as coastal clean-ups and beach patrols and surveys.

sections.label: Biodiversity impact monitoring and research
sections.summary: Impact assessments, post-incident biodiversity monitoring, surveys and research will continue with the nature, scientific and volunteer communities and IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Fourth, we will continue to undertake impact assessments and sustained post-incident biodiversity impact monitoring, surveys and research, in collaboration with the nature community and volunteers, scientific community and our IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Fifth, we will conduct scientific research with the scientific community to better understand the longer-term impacts of the oil spill on biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We have already started surveys at the Southern Islands and Labrador Nature Reserve, as well as Serapong and Tanjong Rimau in Sentosa.

sections.label: Scale of oil spill
sections.summary: An estimated 400 tonnes of oil was spilled into the sea in a sudden discharge, so it is not a small oil spill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second thing is about the scale of the oil spill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is not a small oil spill because we have an estimated 400 tonnes of oil spilled into the sea in a sudden discharge.

sections.label: Clean-up cost and insurer claims
sections.summary: It is too early to confirm clean-up costs, but after operations the total cost will be tallied and claims submitted to the bunker vessel's insurer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Who will eventually bear the cost of this clean-up exercise?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, it is too early for us to confirm what the cost will be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But what we can say in response to Mr Yam's question, in terms of who will bear the cost, is that after the operations are over, we will tally up the total cost for the clean-up and we will submit these claims to the insurer of the bunker vessel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: One, it has been reported that T&T Salvage Asia was mobilised on the same day of the collision at about 2.55 pm and it took them just over 14 hours before they were mobilised and finished laying the 200-metre booms around the Marine Honour.

sections.label: Loading point location and arrival
sections.summary: A loading point in the western or eastern part may not be as centralised as Marina South Wharves, and they arrived at the incident site at 9.41 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, if you were to put your loading point in the western part or in the eastern part, it may not be as centralised as Marina South Wharves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They arrived at the incident site at 9.41 pm.

sections.label: Spilled oil in sea
sections.summary: Oil spilled into the sea, estimated at 400 tonnes, will not stay there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The oil that has been spilled, especially when it is in a large amount, estimated 400 tonnes, sudden discharge into the sea, it will not stay there.

sections.label: Assessing spill response
sections.summary: T&T Salvage Asia did their best and response time was in line with international industry practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, I think it is important for us, as we discuss this matter and as we assess the response, of whether it is MPA or its contractor, in this case T&T Salvage Asia, to bear that in mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I would say, given the weather conditions, nightfall and the amount of work that is required to lay out the booms, I think T&T Salvage Asia did their best and the response time was in line with industry practices internationally.

sections.label: Penalties and insurer liability
sections.summary: Investigations continue before penalties are considered, but the bunker vessel has strict liability and its insurer British Marine must respond to claims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Member Alex Yam mentioned about the cost, but can Minister share a bit about the penalties under the current legislation or Act, whether it commensurate with the cost of clean-up and provides a sufficient deterrent?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are still doing the investigation, so I think we let the investigations be completed before we look at what are the appropriate penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But what remains quite clear is that with or without the penalties under the law, which is subject to the findings of the investigations, the bunker vessel in this case has strict liability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the insurer, British Marine, which is the insurer of the damaged bunker vessel, will have to respond to claims from parties who are affected by this incident.

sections.label: Revolving Fund Committee support
sections.summary: The three littoral states can request and provide support for oil spills and clean-up in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Likewise, when there is an oil spill in their waters, they will also do the same to help us to be able to respond effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And we are part of the Revolving Fund Committee where the three littoral states can request and provide support for oil spills and clean-up operations in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore.

sections.label: Overall spill response
sections.summary: There is no single number for response time, but MPA's patrol vessel arrived in 11 minutes and sprayed dispersants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, because of all those factors, there is not a single number that you can say, "Oh, did you meet this X hours?" It is not quite like that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if we look at the overall response, including the deployment of the MPA patrol vessel arriving 11 minutes, started to spray dispersants, which is very important, I think in the initial period before the oil starts to harden.

sections.label: Booms and oil movement
sections.summary: Even a shorter response would take several hours, by which time currents and waves would carry spilled oil away; booms prevent further spillage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Because even if you talk about a shorter response, because the weather was good and it was not at night and the contractor, the vessel, was able to deploy the booms fully in a quicker way, it would still take several hours at least.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: By that time, the tidal currents and the waves would have already carried the oil that has been spilled into the sea further away from the incident site.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The purpose of the containment booms around the damaged vessel is as a preventive measure to prevent the further oil spillage from coming out from the damaged vessel.

sections.label: Oil patch detection and skimmers
sections.summary: Drones, satellite imagery, ship sightings and anchorage alerts were used to locate oil, and skimmers were deployed on 15 June morning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They used drones, they used satellite imagery, they also used visual sighting from ships, they alerted the ships in our anchorages to try and look out for where the oil patches may be floating to and then they tried to piece together the different information to confirm where is the location of the oil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And when they saw the oil patches on the 15 of June morning, they deployed the oil skimmers to deal with these oil patches.

sections.label: Wave height and tidal current
sections.summary: The wave height was between 0.1 and 0.3 metres and the tidal current was 1.7 knots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The wave height at the time was between 0.1 metres and 0.3 metres and the tidal current was 1.7 knots.

sections.label: Large oil patches identified 15 June
sections.summary: For a variety of reasons, the location of the large oil patches was identified only on the morning of 15 June 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For these variety of reasons, we only managed to identify the location of the large oil patches on the morning of 15 June 2024.

sections.label: No feedback on inhalation effects
sections.summary: No feedback has been received on workers or volunteers suffering ill effects from inhalation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In response to questions from the Member, we have not received any feedback on workers nor volunteers suffering from the ill effects of inhalation.

sections.label: Supervision, volunteers and marine park
sections.summary: Workers are supervised with high competency and experience; the public is urged to volunteer for laborious cleaning; the oil spill has no impact on plans for a second marine park.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, they are supervised with a high degree of competency and experiences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And of course, I think we want them all to work under very safe condition, but it is really hard work, so we would like to really urge the public when it is time for us to volunteer that we would step forward to volunteer with the more laborious type of cleaning, where specialised skills is less involved so that we can actually relieve them of some of the work ahead of us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, the answer to the first question is at this point in time, we continue to assess the impact of the oil spill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There is no impact on our plans for a second marine park in Southern Lazarus and Eastern Kusu.

sections.label: Caution on petrochemicals and beach cleaning
sections.summary: Caution is needed because petrochemicals are involved, and an update may come in a week or two to prepare for further general beach cleaning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But we do just want to put a word of caution here, because we are dealing with petrochemicals and we do want to make sure that it is safe to do so.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We hope to give some update maybe in a week or two's time so that we can prepare for further general cleaning of the beaches.

sections.label: Volunteers for coastal patrols
sections.summary: About 700 of 1,500 volunteers were called to help with coastal patrols, advise the public and watch impacted areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Of the 1,500 volunteers who stepped forward, as I said earlier in my answer, that some 700 volunteers have been called upon to help with coastal patrols, to advise members of the public, to help us keep an eye out for impacted areas.

sections.label: Five collaboration areas decided
sections.summary: A closed-door session decided on five broad areas of collaboration, including wildlife rescue, habitat monitoring, coastal clean-up surveys and oil spill research.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We had a closed-door session to discuss areas where we could collaborate more closely on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And as I said earlier in my answer, there were five broad areas that we decided to embark on, ranging from wildlife rescue to habitat monitoring to coastal clean-up surveys, as well as research into scientific questions on the impact of oil spills.

sections.label: Businesses compiling claim numbers
sections.summary: The Minister-in-charge of Trade Relations encourages affected businesses to start compiling numbers to form a basis of claim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Here I am speaking, really, as the Minister-in-charge of Trade Relations, overseeing SDC as well as our tourism business.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: I would encourage businesses that have been affected, first of all, to start compiling the numbers, so that they can form a basis of claim.

sections.label: Affected businesses contact SDC, STB
sections.summary: Affected businesses without a strong land-based business on affected beaches should contact SDC or the Singapore Tourism Board for individual case review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: If you belong to a category that is affected and, yet, do not have a very strong land-based business on the affected beaches, I would suggest that you get in touch with SDC or the Singapore Tourism Board, so that we can look at your cases individually.

sections.label: Claim option and cash flow help
sections.summary: A claim option exists, and help will be explored to bridge businesses' interim cash flow problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As Ms Hazel Poa has mentioned herself, there is always a solution, there is always the option of making a claim.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We will see how we can help the businesses to bridge that cash flow problem in the interim process.

sections.label: Port operations unaffected after allision
sections.summary: MPA ensured port and shipping operations were unaffected on 14 June, and the incident is not expected to raise shipping costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: First, MPA very quickly ensured that port and shipping operations were not affected on 14 June, soon after the allision occurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So that ships could still come to our anchorages, call at our ports; cargo could still be loaded and unloaded; ships could still continue to have their supplies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I do not think this incident will lead to an increase in shipping costs, because it is affecting two vessels in this case and not something that is structural or systemic.

sections.label: Harbour craft fuel alternatives
sections.summary: Harbour craft plying port waters could use electrification, biofuels, LNG, methanol, ammonia or hydrogen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The harbour craft, which are the vessels that ply within our port waters, this can be done through a mix of electrification and also the use of biofuels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The alternatives that people are looking at would include liquefied natural gas (LNG) and newer types of fuels, like methanol, ammonia and, perhaps, even hydrogen.

sections.label: Oil fencing not practical
sections.summary: International industry practice is not to fence in oil because it is not practical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: During this time, the oil would have floated away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is why the international industry practice is not to try and "fence in" the oil, because it is not practical.

sections.label: Locating and collecting spilled oil
sections.summary: International practice is to locate and collect floated oil, which MPA and contractors did on 15 June.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But for the oil that has floated away, the international practice is to, as quickly as possible, try and locate where the oil is and then to be able to scoop it up, collect it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But as I explained earlier, it took some time before MPA and the contractors were able to confirm the location of the large oil patches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They were only able to do so the next morning, on 15 June, due to bad weather on the first day, the initial part, and then subsequently because of nightfall.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But when they discovered where the oil was, they very quickly deployed the oil skimmers to deal with it.
